study type: Mixed-methods study (qualitative human-centred design and quantitative cross-sectional analysis of administrative data)
exposure: Antimicrobial prophylaxis practices for GBS and SSI prevention
Antibiotic choices for beta-lactam allergic patients (cefazolin, clindamycin, penicillin)
outcome: Gaps and opportunities for clinical improvement
cohort: The study involved seven obstetrical health care providers for journey mapping and 13,818 patients who delivered in Alberta hospital sites between November 1, 2022 and May 31, 2023 for administrative data analysis.
finding: While most patients received appropriate antimicrobial prophylaxis, the study highlighted a need for improved allergy documentation, better penicillin allergy risk stratification, and addressed persistent suboptimal use of second-line antibiotics for penicillin-allergic patients.
